content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity), confidence 0.72.**

**What I found.** Paragraph 18 of the APCN 2 C&MA gives no Party — including Teleglobe USA — any right to exit during the twenty-five (25) year Initial Period:

- **18.1 (p0228)** permits termination of participation only "at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter," on one year's notice.
- **18.2 (p0229)** allows mid-term termination only by unanimous written agreement of all Parties.
- **18.5 (p0233)** forfeits all capital-cost credit for a terminating Party.
- **22.1 (p0246)** blocks assignment or sale of our interest absent Management Committee consent, so there is no back-door exit either.

Under T4C this is walk-away territory: no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term, plus an uncapped exit penalty (full capital-cost forfeiture) well beyond the fallback's three-months'-fees cap. Notably, there is no Vendor-side convenience right to strike — the lock-in is symmetric across the consortium Parties — so the fix is additive rather than subtractive.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** New Subparagraph 18.2A inserted after 18.2 giving any Party a convenience termination right on ninety (90) days' written notice, including during the Initial Period, while preserving liability for accrued Capital Costs and O&M, capping any further exit charge at three months' O&M share, and disapplying the 18.5 capital-cost forfeiture.

**Why fallback rather than preferred.** The preferred 30-day exit with pro-rata refund is disproportionate to this bargain — a shared-asset submarine cable system with continuing Terminal Station obligations under 18.4 and 23.3. The 90-day fallback with a capped exit charge is the defensible ask; the comment flags that we would accept the 30-day/pro-rata formulation if the consortium prefers it.
